key_insight: Simulations suggest calcium channel blockers reduce arterial media stress but shift load to the fibrous cap, potentially increasing plaque rupture risk when blood pressure reduction is insufficient.
engineering_relevance: Coupled drug-transport and arterial-mechanics modeling can reveal local stress trade-offs that smooth muscle relaxation alone does not capture.
method: Couple mechanical equilibrium with 3D reaction–diffusion drug transport.
Model calcium-dependent smooth muscle contraction, anisotropic tissue behavior, and residual stresses.
Fit material parameters to published experiments and run finite element simulations on histology-derived artery geometries.
evidence_signal: Across five geometries, fibrous cap stress increased with median increases up to 28.9 kPa; a 10 mmHg blood pressure reduction limited median increases to at most 3.8 kPa in four geometries.
watch_item: Results are morphology-dependent predictions from five exemplary geometries; the proposed rupture-risk implication requires experimental and clinical validation.
paper_title: Pharmaco-mechanical computational simulation of atherosclerotic arteries: effects of calcium channel blockers on local stress distributions
